title: Chapter 14: Stream Pipelines and Data Processing
description: Design lazy, single-use data pipelines whose types and costs remain understandable. Learners trace source-to-terminal execution, distinguish map from flatMap, prove reduction associativity, build collision-aware and downstream collectors, close resource-backed streams, and reject parallelism when ordering, interference, blocking, or small workloads erase its value.

hints: Intermediate operations such as filter are only recorded lazily; traversal starts when a terminal operation such as count is invoked.

exercises.instructionMarkdown: Which operation flattens nested element streams?
hints: flatMap maps each element to its own stream and flattens all of those streams into one, unlike map which would leave nested streams or arrays.

lessons.title: Reduction, associativity, identity, and primitive streams

exercises.title: Reduction, associativity, identity, and primitive streams: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why is subtraction unsafe as an associative parallel reduction?
choices: Subtraction needs an explicit synchronized block to run safely in parallel
The identity value must be nonzero for reduce to compile
hints: Associativity requires that regrouping operands produce the same result; (a-b)-c differs from a-(b-c) in general, so parallel regrouping is unsafe.

exercises.instructionMarkdown: What must a toMap collector specify when duplicate keys are allowed?
choices: A custom hashCode override on the key type

choices: Closing is needed to start filtering
Its stream owns an external file resource

exercises.title: Chapter 14 implementation lab: evenSquares
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `evenSquares`. Return the sum of the squares of all even integers in the input. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Input is non-null; all squared values and their sum in supplied tests fit int.
hints: Filter for evenness, including negative even numbers and zero, before squaring and accumulating the sum.
Check an empty array, an array with no even numbers, and an array containing a negative even number before submitting.

exercises.title: Flatten words before counting
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Repair the pipeline so per-line word streams are flattened into one stream of words instead of being counted as nested stream objects, and the program writes exactly `3`. Keep the same split-and-count structure and explain why flatMap versus map changes what count() measures, rather than hard-coding the print statement. Output tests verify the printed result; confirming the words are genuinely flattened requires reading the source.
hints: map counts nested streams; flatten them to count words.
